fieldData.meta-description: Build a registration form that takes the fee, stops at your cap, starts a waitlist and saves each registrant to a database you own.
fieldData.name: Build a Registration Form That Manages Every Registrant
fieldData.description: Describe who is signing up and for what. Emergent builds the registration form, takes any fee through Stripe and keeps each registrant as a row in your own database.
fieldData.acrm---key-feature-sub-heading: Collecting a name is the easy part. These six pieces decide whether the list is still right on the day.
fieldData.acrm---key-feature-4-content:
Uploads checked before approval

Ask for a permit or a receipt and hold the registration until someone reviews it. Emergent can read dates and numbers off an upload and flag a file that is missing or out of date.
fieldData.acrm---key-feature-6-content:
Code you can take with you

Publish on your own domain or embed the form on a site you already run. Export the full code to GitHub when a developer wants registrations inside the product your team maintains.

fieldData.awb---integration-feature-1:
A warranty date read straight off the receipt

Buyers of the Kestrel grinder register it with the serial number and a photo of the receipt. The form reads the purchase date off the photo, adds two years and saves the warranty end date to the buyer's contact in HubSpot. A receipt it cannot read goes to the support queue for a person to check.

fieldData.awb---how-to-step-1-des: An event seat and a market booth need different records. Write down what one finished registration looks like as a row: the person, what they registered for, what they paid and any document attached to it.
fieldData.afb---how-to-step-5-des: Paste your notes in plain English: the fields, the caps, the fee and who gets alerted. Emergent builds the form along with the registrant table and the emails around it. Change anything later by asking, such as moving a deadline back a week.
fieldData.afb---how-to-step-7-des: Publish the form on your own domain, or add it to a page people already visit. Put the link where registrants look anyway, such as a newsletter or a QR code at the venue. A daily count in Slack shows how fast spots are going.
